title: Practice: undo and redo misbehave
task: Undo in my to-do app doesn't work properly, and redo does nothing. Here is how it should work. Undo reverses the most recent delete, rename or toggle (done/not done), one action per press, newest first. An undone delete puts the task back exactly where it was in the list, with the same id. Redo re-applies the most recently undone action. Any new delete, rename or toggle clears the redo history. Pressing undo or redo when there is nothing to undo or redo does nothing.

good_edit.text: Rewrite the undo system in todo.py with two stacks, self._undo and self._redo. Every delete/rename/toggle pushes a record onto _undo and clears _redo. Delete records ('delete', index, the whole item dict) and undo re-inserts that same dict at that index (same id, do not call add). Rename records ('rename', id, old_title, new_title). Toggle records ('toggle', id). undo() pops from _undo, reverses it and pushes it onto _redo; redo() pops from _redo, re-applies it and pushes it back onto _undo, without clearing _redo. Both do nothing when their stack is empty.

checks.test_undo_rename: Undo after a rename brings back the old name.
checks.test_undo_delete_same_place_same_id: Undo after a delete puts the task back in the same place, with the same id.
checks.test_undo_toggle: Undo after ticking a task as done un-ticks it.
checks.test_newest_first: Several undos reverse the most recent action first.
checks.test_two_deletes_restore_positions: Undoing two deletes puts both tasks back where they were.
checks.test_redo: Redo re-applies what was just undone.
checks.test_redo_then_undo_again: After a redo, undo works again.
checks.test_new_action_clears_redo: A new action clears redo, so redo does nothing afterwards.
checks.test_empty_undo_redo_do_nothing: Undo or redo with nothing to undo or redo changes nothing.
